scope: Twelve stable guardrails and six affected diagnostics against original main, plus one selected-resize optimization comparison. This is not a final rerun of all 93 initial workloads.
comparison: Three sequential baseline, control and candidate captures per job on the same host and in the same clock mode. Candidate median of three is compared with the lower baseline/control median of three. All 18 original-main comparisons are within 5%; the target optimization gain is at least 5%.

sourceEquivalence.conclusion: Runtime sources and dependency manifests/locks are identical across the measured candidate revisions. Measurement changes add the equally applied SSR sample minimum and optional browser clock mode. Clock modes are never compared against one another.

clockEligibility: Both short browser rows are recaptured with verified isolation and 0.005 ms steps on every source. Their minimum capture medians span 85 and 256 ticks. Other browser rows use the original mode; their shortest capture median is 3.6 ms, spanning 36 observed 0.1 ms steps. Node/jsdom rows do not share that browser quantization constraint.
stability: Runner-source investigation and filename-filtered cleaner recaptures fulfilled the documented response to source-series drift. Residual drift is retained below, including 5.426% in the precise SSR attribute control. The lower-baseline comparison, 5% limits and sample-quality rules are unchanged. No general causal attribution or universal performance claim is made.
